steps.content: An MBCC vehicle pulls up in front of a grandiose manor.
The manor looks like something straight out of a novel or TV drama. An elegant fountain, well-manicured hedges, a cast-iron gate abutting a gilded plate that bears the family name: Golstoy.
But there is a gloomy atmosphere surrounding the manor, impervious to the jauntiness of the dancing water in the fountain.

steps.speaker: Waiter
steps.content: Hello, special representative from the city hall, Mr. ${PlayerName}?
steps.female_content: Hello, Special representative from the city hall, Miss ${PlayerName}?

steps.speaker: Waiter
steps.content: Mrs. Golstoy has been waiting for you. This way please.
The servant leads you to the main building on the property. Along the way, uniformed servants, male or female, whisper when they spot you, all wearing a suspicious look.
Standing by the front door leading into the hall is a lady in exquisite attire.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Sorry about their rudeness.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Who would have thought that they would find a criminal in their ranks?

options: The truth has yet to be unearthed.

choices.text: The truth has yet to be unearthed.

steps.content: That's why I've come.
I'd appreciate your cooperation.
Mrs. Golstoy presses her lips together, and saying nothing further, leads you into the house.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: She is held in her room for lawful detention. The crime scene is being protected by the police.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Feel free to look around, and you can talk to her if you like.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: But it's an ironclad fact that she's guilty. I don't think the presence of a special representative will make any difference.
Mrs. Golstoy puts her handkerchief over her nose, and as if realizing it's inappropriate, lowers her hand. Then she points at somewhere down the hallway.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: It's over there. I'll leave you to it then.
Thank you for leading the way.
Sensing your confusion, she smiles and pushes the document back to you.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: She's the murderer.
Mrs. Golstoy stops in her tracks, turns around, and stares down at you.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: I'm not going to lose this case.

options: It all depends on how the trial will pan out.

choices.text: It all depends on how the trial will pan out.

steps.content: The judge's gavel will bring us the truth.
Mrs. Golstoy falls silent, gives you a cold look, and continues her ascent upstairs.
You approach the bar, near which two police officers keep guard. You show them the document Nightingale got you that identifies you as a special representative, and they stand aside to let you pass.
Mr. Golstoy dropped dead while reading the newspaper at the bar after a meal. Inside the roped-off area is a chalk outline.
Excuse me, could you tell me where the suspect is kept?

steps.speaker: Police Officer A
steps.content: Second room to the left of the bar. It's in fact a bedroom for servants.
Thank you.

steps.speaker: Police Officer A
steps.content: Here's the deal. You can talk to her, but only through the small window in the door. No physical contact. I hope you can understand.

steps.speaker: Police Officer A
steps.content: And the scene... you can look around, but please try not to touch anything.
You look in the direction of the room and see the window in the door. It's a small window that opens outward. You catch a glimpse of the inside of the room.
She lives in a room like that? It's just a glorified prison cell.

steps.speaker: Police Officer B
steps.content: Some rich people can be very mistrustful. And they're not wrong, considering what's transpired here.

steps.speaker: Police Officer B
steps.content: She looks delicate. I didn't know she had it in her. But even a worm turns. Maybe the man was asking for it...
Dissing a dead man in the middle of the day... Officer, you're not worried it might bring you bad luck?

steps.speaker: Police Officer B
steps.content: Heh... go ahead and look around, sir.
steps.female_content: Heh... go ahead and look around, miss.

steps.content: You pull on the gloves and shoe covers the officer handed you, and start inspecting the dining hall.

The police combed the scene after Mrs. Golstoy reported the death of her husband. You've looked through the physical evidence the police gathered, but noticed nothing particularly suspicious—you have a feeling that it was made to look that way.
The victim started his meal at around eight o'clock. By then, the hard-working maids had cleaned the dining hall inside out.
As your eyes sweep around the hall, you catch sight of a nearby table on which are displayed seasoning jars of different sizes.
What's this? <color=#fb9259>Two identical jars</color> of seasoning?
You pick them up and open one of them. Inside the jar are fine white crystals, probably table sugar.
Inside the other jar are also white crystals, finer than those in the first jar, but the substance doesn't smell like a seasoning.
You produce an evidence bag and shake some of the substance into the bag.

steps.speaker: Police Officer A
steps.content: Special representative...
You said try not to touch anything.
I tried, but without success.
You've inspected the dining table. The chalk outline, water stains, a flower arrangement, wine bottles, and cartons of cigarettes... these are things left on the table.
To the right and near the top of the chalk outline is an open box of cigars lying next to a gray <color=#fb9259>cigar cutter</color>, which is attached to an expensive-looking leather string.

There's a small pile of broken glass lying not far away from the edge of the carpet. At the time, Mr. Golstoy, weak and losing consciousness, must have thrown the glass against the wall and shattered it.
Although the glass was shattered and it had been empty when Mr. Golstoy threw it, the police managed to detect in a few drops of liquid what might have been the drug that killed Mr. Golstoy.
This piece of evidence might have led the police to believe that the maid was the culprit...
Drug poisoning?
You notice the whiskey bottle beside the dining table. Less than one third is left in the bottle. Mr. Golstoy must have been in the habit of using a drink or two every now and again.
As you reach out, you bump against the table, which wobbles with a grating noise. The picture frame falls face-down on the table.
Hmm?
A shabby table in a rich household... That's strange.

steps.speaker: Police Officer B
steps.content: Sir, look where you're putting your feet! Be careful not to break anything. Please don't make trouble for us.
steps.female_content: Miss, look where you're putting your feet! Be careful not to break anything. Please don't make trouble for us.

steps.content: The carpet in the dining hall is a light color， seemingly to create a nice atmosphere for the diners.
But there are patches that look sticky and stiffened, courtesy of some repulsive liquid.
You gauge the distances, trying to figure out how the liquid landed on the carpet. And then you come upon a patch with some strange stains on it when you get near the midsection of the dining table.
It's so far away... The liquid couldn't have landed here.
You cut the stiffened patch off the carpet with a pair of scissors and bring it to your nose.
You smell a hint of artificial essence mixed with something that is hard to put into words. You sigh when you realize what it might be.
Still going at it like a young stallion?

You take a final look at the stained piece of material before putting it in an evidence bag, which you'll give to Nightingale. She'll order a test run on it and report the results back to you as soon as they're available.
Having inspected the scene, you pick up the fallen picture frame and replace it.

I remember him. He's Golstoy Junior, right?

steps.speaker: Police Officer A
steps.content: Yes. But his birth mother isn't the current Mrs. Golstoy.

steps.speaker: Police Officer B
steps.content: I heard it's a difficult birth, and there's fetal hypoxia. Golstoy Junior was born with mental disabilities, and his birth mother died in childbirth. He is an adult now, but there's something not quite right here.
The officer indicates what's wrong with Golstoy Junior by tapping his finger on the side of his own head.
I see...

steps.speaker: Police Officer B
steps.content: Women came and went as Mr. Golstoy strove for a healthy heir. God knows how many Mrs. Golstoys have come before the current one!
The other officer gives the arm of his partner a tug. He probably thinks that his partner is being flippant and talking too much.
Thank you for telling me this.
You nod at the police officers and come to the door of the room where the maid is kept. Looking through the window, you see her sitting in a chair.
She keeps fiddling with the edge of her apron, looking so high-strung that it's almost painful to watch.
Hello...
You knock on the door. Like a startled rabbit, she whips around in her seat, lips trembling. When she sees you standing outside the door, she jumps to her feet.

steps.speaker: Maid
steps.content: S-sorry, sir.
steps.female_content: S-sorry, miss.

steps.speaker: Maid
steps.content: I... I'm here. What can I do for you?
No need to worry. I just want to ask you a few questions.

steps.speaker: Maid
steps.content: Are you... are you here to prove my innocence?
The law and evidence will prove it, if you really are innocent, that is.

steps.speaker: Maid
steps.content: You're the first person who has ever shown any interest in hearing my side of the story...
I hope you can answer my questions honestly, miss.

steps.speaker: Maid
steps.content: Rita, you can call me Rita, sir.
steps.female_content: Rita, you can call me Rita, miss.

steps.content: Rita, did you spike Mr. Golstoy's whisky?

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: I... I did. But I did it because...
Rita clasps her hands together in front of her chest, as if in prayer, eager to explain herself.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Mr. Golstoy was not feeling well. He complained of widespread body aches. It was an old illness. I was the one handling his medicines. But this particular medicine was too bitter, so Mr. Golstoy was not very willing to take it.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Mrs. Golstoy, she told me to dissolve the medicine in alcohol and let Mr. Golstoy drink it. That's why I did it.
In any case, it's wrong to let a patient take medicine with alcohol.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: I... I didn't know you're not supposed to mix medicine with alcohol. I just followed Mrs. Golstoy's order.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: This new Mrs. Golstoy is quite overbearing. We're all kind of scared of her. We do whatever she tells us.
New Mrs. Golstoy?

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Yes, she moved in only five months ago.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Sir, I dared not make any attempt on Mr. Golstoy's life, not in a million years. I'm just a nobody at the bottom of the pile, as insignificant as a creepy-crawly...
steps.female_content: Miss, I dared not make any attempt on Mr. Golstoy's life, not in a million years. I'm just a nobody at the bottom of the pile, as insignificant as a creepy-crawly...

steps.content: Rest assured, neither money nor someone's... special power can tip Lady Justice's scales in their favor.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: A-are you telling me that I can trust you, sir?
steps.female_content: A-are you telling me that I can trust you, miss?

steps.content: Rita's mouth tightens into a thin line, and the outer edges of her eyes turn downward. She reaches out and puts her hand on the small window.
Miss Rita, all I can say is I'm at the service of law and morality.
The look in her eyes turns solemn. Before you can say anything more, someone darts in to stand between you and the door.
Bad person? You... bad person?

steps.speaker: Police Officer A
steps.content: Sorry. He burst in, and we didn't dare stop him.
The unexpected visitor has dull, empty eyes that somehow chill you. His clothes are disheveled but evidently made of fine material.
You recognize him: Mr. Golstoy's son, Golstoy Junior. No wonder the police officers didn't dare to stop him.
I don't think I'm a bad person, Master Golstoy.
Sorry about your father... My condolences.
If you have anything you want to share with me, please do so...

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: Bad... Bad person hits me, shouts at me, lets... lets the rat bite my fingers... Bad person…
Who is this bad person? Who hits you and shouts at you?
You don't want your questions to stress the young man out, so you soften your tone.
The young man seems to be pondering your questions, remembering. He is murmuring, eyes downcast and unfocused, hands on the head.

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: It hurts, it hurts... the rat bites my fingers... it hurts...

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: Rita... Rita doesn't let the rat bite my fingers...

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: She gives me milk. She is a good person.

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: She heats milk, hot milk for me, for... for Daddy.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Master!
She growls at the young man, her voice uncharacteristically stern. You and Golstoy Junior turn to her.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Sorry, sir. I'm also the one who takes care of Master Golstoy in his daily life.
steps.female_content: Sorry, miss. I'm also the one who takes care of Master Golstoy in his daily life.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: I'm locked up, and there are so many strangers around. He must be scared. Please forgive both of us...
It's okay. Innocent people tend to tell the truth. I'd like to talk some more with him.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: But, um, he's scared. He can't speak clearly now. Please let him go back and rest.
Rita's comforting words seem to have calmed Golstoy Junior down. He looks at you, and then at Rita, before following the officer out of the dining hall.
Having gathered the information you need, you leave the property. As you drive out, you see another black sedan. Then one of the opaque rear windows is rolled down.
The man in the back seat smiles at you.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Chief, are you going to represent Miss Rita?
I could ask for a certificate allowing me to represent the defender.
But I don't think that's the right thing to do.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: You should use whatever tool at your disposal to get what you want.
Mr. Fox shrugs, as if he has just told you something mundane.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Of course, I don't mind you watching me killing it in court as a spectator.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Chief, thank you for your understanding. See you around.
See you. My understanding doesn't come free.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: I can't wait.
The next day...

Eastside's supreme court. To protect the privacy of the Golstoy family, one of the noble families in Eastside, the trial is not being held in open court. You, as a special representative, are now sitting in the far corner of the spectator area.
Mrs. Golstoy and Mr. Fox are sitting at the plaintiff's table, which seems better illuminated than the defendant's table.

Rita, the poor maid, is at the defendant's table, uneasy and troubled, the way she was the last time you saw her, sitting in that chair in that cramped room, a room in which she has lived and to which she has been confined.

No one wanted to represent her. In a humanitarian gesture, the court appointed a lawyer to represent her. Now, the lawyer is turning the pages of a document, looking as if he's got nothing better to do.
He has sighed five times in three minutes.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Eastside's supreme court. We now will begin the case of the Golstoy manor.
The judge pounds the gavel. The air in the room is heavy with tension, and everyone is perceptibly on edge, except for Fox.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Allow me to recapitulate on this case.
Fox stands up, adjusts his glasses, and casts a glance in your direction.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Mr. Golstoy died two days ago in the dining hall of his manor. According to the autopsy report, Mr. Golstoy suffered no traumas or fatal injuries, but his blood pH was off the charts, a clear sign of acidosis.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: He also suffered a cardiac arrest, so after considering all the factors, the forensic experts determined the cause of death as acidic drug-induced acute toxicity.
Mr. Fox shows the room the autopsy report, on which a conspicuous red stamp proclaims the authenticity of the report.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: We have good reason to suspect you, Miss Rita. It had always been you who handled Mr. Golstoy's medicine. If anyone had the opportunity to tamper with his medicine, it was you.
Fox gives a slight nod and puts on a vulpine smile, delivering his conclusion with finality.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: In conclusion, you, Miss Rita, murdered Mr. Golstoy.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Miss Rita, you said you're as insignificant as a creepy-crawly...

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: But are you a harmless earthworm, or a poisonous centipede that bites?
Miss Rita turns ashen. She opens her mouth to say something, but nothing comes out.

steps.speaker: Defendant's Lawyer
steps.content: She can't benefit from the death of her employer.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: There isn't always a logical reason for such behavior. Humans are cruel creatures... It's a good thing that we have lawyers. We exist to get to the bottom of a case and bring the culprit to justice.
Fox turns to the judge and asks to call the first witness.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: To prove that Miss Rita had the chance to poison her employer and did take advantage of the chance, I'd like to call one of Miss Rita's colleagues to the stand.
A girl in a uniform similar to Rita's approaches the witness stand, casting nervous looks at Fox.

steps.speaker: Maid A
steps.content: H-hi, everyone...

steps.speaker: Maid A
steps.content: I had nothing to do with it, really... There's nothing special about the foods Mr. Golstoy had that day, just the usual, and what Mr. Golstoy would eat was decided beforehand.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Miss, you needn't worry. Just tell us what you know.

steps.speaker: Maid A
steps.content: But... But I... I...
The maid on the stand stammers, eyes blinking. Finally, she hangs her head and resumes giving testimony. She sounds as if she's talking to herself.

steps.speaker: Maid A
steps.content: I... I'm not entirely sure, but I think I saw Rita pour some powder into Mr. Golstoy's drink. We did the dishes together after breakfast that day.

steps.speaker: Maid A
steps.content: And the night before, I also saw her add something to the milk she was heating in the dining hall. It was also some kind of powder, I think...

steps.speaker: Maid A
steps.content: Later that night, it was in Mr. Golstoy's bedroom that I saw a milk glass, and I took it outside.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: It's sugar. I added sugar to the milk!

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Admit it, Miss Rita! You didn't succeed with the milk, so the next day, you spiked the drink.
Rita's clenched fists are shaking. She can't think of anything else to defend herself.
This may not be the case.
You rise to your feet. Fox narrows his eyes at you, staring at you as if you were a prey.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: This is...?

steps.speaker: Defendant's Lawyer
steps.content: Oh, he's a special representative sent by the authorities, but I don't know why they sent him…
steps.female_content: Oh, she's a special representative sent by the authorities, but I don't know why they sent her...

steps.content: I'm a special representative from the City Council. Some aspects of this case may fall within the City Council's jurisdiction, so I was sent down here to take care of them.
In light of what's happened, I wish to argue the case with this... lawyer.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: ...Go ahead then, special representative from the City Council.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: But next time, please follow the normal procedure if you wish to speak. Now, please come to the witness stand, sir.
steps.female_content: But next time, please follow the normal procedure if you wish to speak. Now, please come to the witness stand, miss.

steps.content: You make to take the witness stand, but Fox comes up to you.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: It didn't surprise me to see you here, but I didn't expect that you'd take the stand.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Am I supposed to take it as a challenge?
Fox chuckles. You seem to glimpse a hint of craziness in his reddish eyes.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Haha, very well, very well... I used my power against you in our last encounter, and it took a great toll on my mind. I don't think I'll be able to use my power again any time soon.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: But that's for the better. Since I can't use my power, there's no reason for you to use the shackles.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: This way, we can fight it out on a level playing field. I accept your challenge. May the best person win!

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: It's been so long since I felt so...
Fox doesn't finish his sentence. He looks at you for a long while before stepping aside to let you go up to the witness stand.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Tell us your theory then, sir.
steps.female_content: Tell us your theory then, miss.
